results.description:
Christmas Never Have I Ever is the classic confession game turned into a fingers-down holiday party game for the whole crowd. Everyone holds up ten fingers, someone reads a card that starts with "Never have I ever...", and anyone who has done it puts a finger down. Last finger standing wins. Two decks, one for the whole family and one for the grown-ups, plus a candy-betting bonus round. No drinking needed, ever.

INSTANT DOWNLOAD · Printable PDF in US Letter + A4 · Nothing will be shipped.

What's included
- Cover + one-page How to Play with house rules and a "print only what you use" checklist
- Family deck: 36 illustrated cards (cookies, carols, presents, broken ornaments). Safe for kids 8+ and Grandma
- Grown-Ups deck: 36 illustrated cards (re-gifting, office parties, in-laws, December 23rd shopping). Cheeky, never explicit, nothing sexual
- Glove scorecards: 4 per page, cross off a finger for every "I have" (great for big groups or tired arms)
- Speed Round host sheet: 28 rapid-fire prompts, stand up if you've done it
- Ever or Never candy round: rules page with a betting board, 6 fold-over EVER / NEVER vote cards and a 20-line Hot Seat checklist
- "Last Finger Standing" winner certificate (The Innocent One or The Legend)
- 120 prompts, 20 pages in US Letter and A4

Who it's for: families with kids and teens, holiday parties with friends, office and team parties, grandparents, game nights and virtual parties. 3 to 20 players.

1. Print the deck you want (or both) on cardstock and cut the cards. Print the other games only if you'll play them.
2. Everyone holds up ten fingers. Take turns reading a card: "Never have I ever..." Done it? Put one finger down.
3. Out of fingers? You're out, and you owe the table one story. The last player with a finger up wins the certificate. Play Ever or Never or the Speed Round for an encore.

Sizes included: US Letter (8.5 x 11 in) and A4 (210 x 297 mm), high-resolution PDF. Every page has print-safe margins for home printers.

Printing tip: Print at 100% / Actual size. Use cardstock (65-110 lb) for the cards, vote cards and certificate; plain paper is fine for the score and host sheets. Light backgrounds keep ink use low. Put the glove scorecards in sheet protectors and use a dry-erase marker to play again.
